results.title: The norm on $F(T)$

results.title: Fixed points of maps whose iterates have null Lipschitz constants

results.summary: Let $X$ be a nonempty complete metric space, let $f : X \to X$, and write $f^n$ for the $n$-th iterate of $f$. results.summary: A deterministic Turing machine $M$ with $k$ work tapes is space bounded by $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ when, for every input word $w$, every computation path of $M$ on $w$ visits at most $s(|w|)$ work-tape cells, counting the cells visited on each work tape and summing over the tapes, where $|w|$ is the length of $w$.

results.summary: Let $M$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $w$ be an input word and let $T \in \mathbb{N}$. results.title: Uniform time bounds give uniform space bounds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes and let $t : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. If $M$ is time bounded by $t$, then $M$ is space bounded by the function $n \mapsto k(t(n) + 1)$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t_1, t_2 : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $t_1(n) \le a \, t_2(n) + b$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $\mathrm{DTIME}(t_1) \subseteq \mathrm{DTIME}(t_2)$.

results.title: The cell of a number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The cell of a natural number $n$ is the list of bits consisting of $n$ copies of the bit true (units) followed by one bit false (a marker).

results.title: The cells of a list of numbers
results.caption: Definition

results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Every stack $k$ of the clocked universal machine holds bits: its alphabet is $\Gamma(k) = \mathrm{Bool}$.

results.title: Decoding units
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The unit decoder sends the bit true (a unit) to the bit true, and sends the bit false (a marker) to no bit, which ends a block.

results.title: Moving a marker onto the scan buffer
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a label $\ell$, this instruction pops the top symbol of the code stack $C$ and discards it (doing nothing if $C$ is empty), pushes a marker (the bit false) onto the scan buffer $B$, and goes to $\ell$; the state bit is unchanged.

results.title: The clocked universal program
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The program of the clocked universal machine gives an instruction for every label. Numbers sit on stacks as counters of units (the bit true), and a cell is a counter followed by a marker (the bit false).

results.title: Entries of a code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a code $c$, the list of quadruples $(q, a, q', s)$, one for each state $q$ and symbol $a$ inside the table of $c$ whose table entry is a transition $(q', s)$ (enter the state $q'$ and do the action coded by $s$); halting positions are skipped. The quadruples are listed row by row, by increasing $q$, and within a row by increasing $a$.

results.title: Looking up a key in a list of entries
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $q$ and $a$ and a list of quadruples $(q_i, a_i, q'_i, s_i)$ of natural numbers, the result is the pair $(q'_i, s_i)$ of the first quadruple in the list with $q_i = q$ and $a_i = a$, and no result if no quadruple has the key $(q, a)$. This is the order in which the machine scans the code stack.

results.title: Scanning the entries finds the table entry
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every code $c$ and all natural numbers $q$ and $a$, looking up the key $(q, a)$ in the entries of $c$ gives the entry of the table of $c$ at state $q$ and symbol $a$: the pair $(q', s)$ if that position holds the transition $(q', s)$, and no result if it halts, including every position outside the table.

results.title: Numbers of a list of entries
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list of quadruples of natural numbers, the list of natural numbers obtained by replacing each quadruple $(q, a, q', s)$ by the four numbers $q, a, q', s$ in this order, keeping the order of the quadruples.

results.caption: Definition

results.title: Existence of a least finite support
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A least finite support exists: among the supports of `x`, one is contained in every support. The proof is by strong induction on a chosen support `S₀`: either every element of `S₀` lies in every support (so `S₀` itself is least), or some `a ∈ S₀` is missing from a support `Sₐ`, and the induction hypothesis applies to the strictly smaller support `Sₐ ∩ S₀`.

results.title: Least finite support of an element
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The *least* finite support of `x`: a support contained in every support of `x`.

results.title: Least support is a support
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The least support is a support.

results.title: Minimality of the least support
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The least support is contained in every support: minimality.

results.title: Membership in the least support
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Membership in the least support: `a ∈ supp (Atom := Atom) x` iff `a` lies in every support of `x`.

results.title: Freshness is non-membership in the least support
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Freshness is exactly non-membership in the least support.

results.title: Equivariance of the least support
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Support is equivariant: permuting `x` permutes its support.

results.title: Support of an atom
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The support of an atom is its singleton.

results.title: Permutations agreeing on the support act equally
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Two permutations that agree on the support of `x` act equally on `x`: their ratio fixes the support pointwise, hence fixes `x`.

results.title: Equivariant elements of a nominal set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An element fixed by every permutation has the empty set as a support.

results.title: Equivariant elements are supported by the empty set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An equivariant element is supported by the empty set.

results.title: Equivariant elements have empty support
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An equivariant element has empty support.

results.title: α-equivalence relation on atom–element pairs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: α-equivalence relation on atom–element pairs. α-equivalence: equal pairs, or a renaming of the bound atom by a fresh transposition.

results.title: Reflexivity of α-equivalence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Reflexivity of α-equivalence. α-equivalence is reflexive.

results.title: Symmetry of α-equivalence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Symmetry of α-equivalence. α-equivalence is symmetric. Symmetry uses equivariance of support (`supp_smul`).

results.title: Transitivity of α-equivalence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Transitivity of α-equivalence. α-equivalence is transitive. Transitivity uses the fact that two permutations agreeing on `supp y` act equally on `y` (`smul_eq_of_agree_on_supp`).

results.title: Setoid of α-equivalence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The setoid of α-equivalence.

results.title: Atom abstraction of a nominal set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Atom abstraction: `[a]x`, the quotient of `Atom × X` by α-equivalence.

results.title: Abstraction of an element at a bound atom
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The abstraction `[a]x`.

results.title: Equality of abstractions is α-equivalence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Equality of abstractions is α-equivalence.

results.title: Abstractions with the same bound atom have equal bodies
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An abstraction with the same bound atom determines its body.

results.title: Permutation action on abstractions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The action of a permutation on abstractions, applied to a representative.

results.title: Permutation action on abstractions computed on representatives
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A permutation applied to an abstraction, on representatives.

results.title: Abstractions are supported by the body's support minus the atom
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The action of a permutation on an abstraction fixes it when the permutation fixes `supp x \ {a}` pointwise.

results.title: Support of an atom abstraction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The support of an abstraction is the body's support minus the bound atom.

results.title: Set partitions of a labeled sample
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The set partitions of a sample of `n` labeled genes `{0, …, n - 1}`.

results.title: Partition obtained by merging two blocks
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: `π'` arises from `π` by merging two blocks: `π` refines `π'` and has exactly one more block (so exactly two blocks of `π` lie in one block of `π'`, and the others are blocks of `π'`).

results.title: Jump chain of Kingman's coalescent
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The transition matrix of the jump chain of Kingman's coalescent: from a partition with `k ≥ 2` blocks, move to each of the `k.choose 2` partitions obtained by merging two blocks with probability `1 / k.choose 2`; a partition with at most one block is absorbing.

results.title: Law of Kingman's jump chain after m jumps
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The law of the jump chain after `m` jumps, started from the partition into singletons: `jumpLaw n m π` is the probability that the partition after `m` coalescences is `π`.

results.title: Kingman's formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The probability `(n - k)! k! (k - 1)! ∏_{B ∈ π} |B|! / (n! (n - 1)!)` of a partition `π` with `k` blocks of a sample of size `n` (meaningful for `1 ≤ k ≤ n`; for the empty sample it gives `1` to the empty partition).

results.title: Rate matrix of Kingman's partition-valued coalescent
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The rate matrix of Kingman's partition-valued coalescent: each pair of blocks merges at rate `1`, so a partition with `k` blocks is left at total rate `k.choose 2` (time in units of `2N` generations).

results.title: Time-t marginal of Kingman's coalescent
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The time-`t` marginal of Kingman's `n`-coalescent started from singletons: `timeLaw n t π = exp (t • partitionRate n) ⊥ π` is the probability that the ancestral partition of the sample at time `t ≥ 0` (in units of `2N` generations) is `π`. The matrix exponential is defined for every real `t`; the identities below hold for every real `t`.

results.title: Restriction matrix on sample partitions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The restriction map as a `0/1` matrix: entry `(π, ρ)` is `1` iff `π.comap Fin.castSucc = ρ`.

results.title: Mergers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A partition with `k` blocks has exactly `k.choose 2` partitions that arise from it by merging two blocks.

results.title: Splitting identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Summing `∏_{B ∈ π} |B|!` over the partitions `π` that merge to `π'` gives `(n - #π'.parts) / 2 · ∏_{B ∈ π'} |B|!`: a block of size `b` has `(2^b - 2) / 2` splits into two blocks, and `∑_{∅ ≠ A ⊊ B} |A|! |B \ A|! = (b - 1) b!`.

results.title: Kingman's formula at the partition into singletons
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Kingman's formula gives probability `1` to the partition into singletons.

results.title: Kingman's formula for a partition with k blocks
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Kingman's formula for a partition with `k` blocks.

results.title: Backward equation of Kingman's formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a partition `π'` with `k` blocks, `1 ≤ k < n`, the Kingman probabilities of the partitions merging to `π'` sum to `(k + 1).choose 2` times the Kingman probability of `π'`.

results.title: Kingman's jump-chain matrix is row-stochastic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The jump-chain transition matrix is row-stochastic.

results.title: Kingman's formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Kingman's formula (Kingman 1982; Durrett 2008, ch. 1). For `m < n`, after `m` coalescences the jump chain started from singletons is at a partition `π` with probability `kingmanProb n π = (n - k)! k! (k - 1)! ∏_{B ∈ π} |B|! / (n! (n - 1)!)` if `π` has `k = n - m` blocks, and `0` otherwise. (For `m ≥ n - 1` the chain has been absorbed at the one-block partition.)

results.title: Jump-chain law sums to one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The jump chain's law after `m` jumps sums to one (its entries are nonnegative by `jumpMatrix_mem_rowStochastic`).

results.title: Kingman's formula is a probability distribution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Kingman's formula is a probability distribution on the partitions with `k` blocks, for `1 ≤ k ≤ n`. Equivalently, `∑_{π, k blocks} ∏_{B ∈ π} |B|! = n! (n - 1)! / ((n - k)! k! (k - 1)!)`, the Lah number `L(n, k)`.

results.title: Kingman's formula is invariant under relabeling
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Relabeling the sample by a permutation (`Finpartition.comap`) preserves Kingman's formula.

results.title: Exchangeability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Exchangeability of the jump chain: for `m < n`, relabeling the sample does not change the probability of a partition after `m` coalescences.

results.title: Number of blocks of a sample partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number of blocks of a partition of a sample of `n`, as an element of `Fin (n + 1)` (a state of the block-counting process).

results.title: Kingman's formula arranged by number of blocks
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Kingman's formula arranged by number of blocks: entry `(k, π)` is `kingmanProb n π` if `π` has `k` blocks and `0` otherwise. For `1 ≤ k ≤ n`, row `k` is the law of the jump chain after `n - k` jumps (`jumpLaw_eq`).

results.title: Last row of Kingman's matrix is the singleton point mass
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Row `n` of `kingmanMatrix n` is the point mass at the partition into singletons.

results.title: Kingman's formula intertwines the block-counting generator with the partition rate matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Kingman's formula intertwines the block-counting generator with the partition rate matrix: `G * Λ = Λ * Q`. This is the backward equation `sum_kingmanProb_isMerge` in matrix form.

results.title: The time-`t` marginal of the partition-valued coalescent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The time-`t` marginal of the partition-valued coalescent (Kingman 1982): for every real `t`, the probability of a partition `π` with `k` blocks is the probability that the block-counting process goes from `n` to `k` lineages in time `t`, times Kingman's formula.

results.title: Time-t marginal via Tavaré's formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The time-`t` marginal with Tavaré's closed form for the block-counting factor: for a partition `π` of a sample of `n` (so `π` has at least one block when `n ≥ 1`), `P(Π_t = π) = tavareProb n k t · kingmanProb n π` with `k = #π.parts`.

results.title: Exchangeability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Exchangeability of the time-`t` marginal.

results.title: Rows of the partition rate matrix sum to zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Each row of the partition rate matrix sums to `0`: a partition with `k` blocks has `k.choose 2` mergers (`card_isMerge`), each at rate `1`.

results.title: Partition rate matrix is a rate matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The partition rate matrix is a rate matrix: off-diagonal entries are `0` or `1`, and each row sums to `0` (`sum_partitionRate`).

results.title: Time-t marginal as a continuous-time chain transition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `timeLaw` is a row of the transition function `P t = exp (t • partitionRate n)` of the continuous-time chain with rate matrix `partitionRate n`.

results.title: Partition coalescent transition matrix is row-stochastic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `t ≥ 0` the transition matrix `exp (t • partitionRate n)` is row-stochastic.

results.title: Nonnegativity of the time-t marginal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `t ≥ 0` the time-`t` marginal is nonnegative; with `sum_timeLaw` it is a probability distribution on the partitions of the sample.

results.title: Time-t marginal sums to one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The time-`t` marginal sums to one over all partitions: `∑_π timeLaw n t π = 1` (for every real `t`, since the rows of the rate matrix sum to `0`).

results.title: Lumpability of restriction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Lumpability of restriction (Kingman 1982): restricting to the first `n` genes intertwines the rate matrices of the `(n + 1)`- and `n`-coalescents.

results.title: Consistency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Consistency (Kingman 1982): the time-`t` law of the restriction of the `(n + 1)`-coalescent to the first `n` genes is the time-`t` law of the `n`-coalescent.

results.title: Path probability of the Kingman coalescent jump chain
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The probability that the jump chain of Kingman's `n`-coalescent, started from the partition into singletons, follows the list of partitions `l`: `0` unless `l` starts at the partition into singletons, and otherwise the product of the one-step transition probabilities `jumpMatrix n` along `l`. The empty list has probability `0`.

results.title: Consistency of the jump chains
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Consistency of the jump chains (Kingman 1982): for `n ≥ 1`, restricting each partition of a path of the `(n + 1)`-jump chain (a list of `n + 1` partitions) to the first `n` genes and deleting consecutive repetitions gives a list of `n` partitions of `Fin n` distributed as the path of the `n`-jump chain.
